title.narrative: Activity under preparation Circular Economy in Central America

description.narrative: Central America faces a significant challenge of material loss and waste management across three priority waste streams: e-waste, agricultural biomass and plastic waste. These materials are often discarded, burned or exported without value recovery, resulting in environmental degradation, public health risks, methane emissions, pollution of rivers and coastlines, and rising costs for municipalities and ecosystems. The challenge is compounded by fragmented regulatory frameworks, reliance on informal waste workers, and limited access to finance for circular economy solutions. The EU can offer Central America an integrated political, industrial, and financial partnership to advance the circular economy. This means supporting policy and regulatory alignment, facilitating access to European technology and expertise, and mobilising private sectors and investors to attract sustainable financing. In this context, Specific objective 1 of this action aims to generate technical, commercial, and financial evidence through the development and demonstration of commercially viable circular economy anchor models. Specific objective 2 aims to strengthen the enabling environment for replication and investment by identifying scalable circular economy pilot projects, fostering partnerships between EU and local actors, developing investment proposals, and reinforcing regulatory and institutional frameworks for scale-up. The action will systematically promote decent work by supporting the formalisation of informal employment, improving working conditions, and promoting gender equality and the inclusion of vulnerable groups in line with the Global Gateway 360-degree approach. Together, these tools can help position the region as a more integrated, investable, and sustainable market connected to European value chains and standards.Designed as a Global Gateway accelerator, the action complements bilateral initiatives under the EU¿LAC Global Gateway Investment Agenda by promoting regulatory convergence, building an investment-ready pipeline, and fostering scalable business partnerships, with the aims to strengthen regional integration and facilitate EU investment in line with the EU¿Central America Association Agreement. Emphasis will be put on strengthening regional e-waste processing while securing EU private sector engagement and off-take agreements for recovered materials; scaling biomass valorisation by replicating inclusive models that convert agricultural residues into circular solutions and connect them to EU bio-based technologies and markets; and post-consumer plastics.The action directly aligns with the Regional Multiannual Indicative Programme for Latin America and the Caribbean (2021¿2027), particularly Priority Area 1: Green Transition (Specific Objective 3: Tackle pollution and accelerate the circular economy) and the Central America Sub-Window¿s "Green and Blue Recovery" goal. It also advances SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 8 (Decent Work), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure).
